images.source: Editorial still life on a calm Daylight background, seen at eye level from slightly above. Three plinths folded from flat faceted paper in white and pale blue-grey stand in a loose row across the lower half, each a little different in height, their tops bare and clean: space kept ready for results that are not in yet. A satin ribbon in a gradient from Alliance Blue to Ribbon Cyan runs in a loose, gentle curve across the front of the plinths from the lower left and rises toward the upper right, like a ribbon waiting to be cut at an opening. A few small faceted paper leaves rest on the ribbon where it touches the floor. The upper half is calm, open Daylight. Nearly square, about 1:1 (604x560), safe to crop to 4:5 (358x420) around the centre. Palette only: Partner Navy #121B2A, Alliance Blue #1B56FF, Ribbon Cyan #00D5FF, Daylight #F4F7FB and the shades between them. Nature built from satin ribbon and flat paper facets. Light from the upper left, soft navy-tinted shadows falling down and to the right. No text or letters, no people, no hands, no robots, no brains, no circuit boards, no sparkles, no glow, no purple or pink, no regional or cultural motifs, no real places or landmarks.

sections.lead: Every case study follows the same four parts, so each one is quick to read and easy to check.

items.title: The problem
items.text: What was slow or stuck, what it cost the partner, and what they had tried before.

items.title: What we did
items.text: The four steps: understand, plan, build, run and grow. We say so when part of the fix needed no AI.

items.title: The results

items.title: In the partner’s words

sections.name: Rules
sections.job: Hold case studies to the price-claim rules in a form a reader can check: real partners, their own numbers, a source and a date for every result, approved before it goes up.
sections.heading: Four rules for every case study. (set on two lines: ‘Four rules for’ / ‘every case study.’)
sections.lead: A case study is a claim about results, so it follows the same rules as our prices: real numbers, each with a source and a date.

items.title: Real partners, real work.
items.text: Every case study is about a partner we worked with and work we did. Samples, like the sample report, are marked as samples.

items.title: Measured in their numbers.
items.text: Before we start, we agree with the partner on what success looks like, using their own numbers. The case study reports against those.

items.title: A source and a date for every result.
items.text: Each result says where the figure came from, such as the partner’s order system, and when it was measured.

items.title: Approved before it goes up.
items.text: The partner reads the whole case study and approves every word, figure and quote before we publish it.

sections.name: Until then
sections.job: Give the reader something real to look at now: the sample report, the AI check-up and a person to talk to.
sections.heading: Until then, see what we find. (mobile set on two lines: ‘Until then,’ / ‘see what we find.’)
sections.lead: The sample report shows what the AI check-up delivers, written for a fictional company. A real check-up does the same for your business.

items.title: The sample report
items.text: Four opportunities ranked by what each would save, a fixed quote for the first fix, and where we would not use AI. Every figure is a placeholder, so nothing in it reads as a real result.

items.title: Book an AI check-up
items.text: Our usual first project: a short review of where AI could save your team time or money, with a report like the sample.

items.title: Talk to a person first
items.text: Tell us what slows your team down, and a person from our team will reply.

notes: Honest empty state: no partner names, logos, quotes, results or numbers anywhere; every bracketed item is a placeholder and the only card is labelled by its brackets and the note under it. One Primary (the hero); the header keeps its Secondary outline and no nav item is marked current, since Case studies is not in the main nav. The ribbon signature appears once (the rule on the placeholder card). One image slot (simple page). The sample report preview repeats the real ranked rows from page 34 so the two pages agree. The four rules come from the Brand DNA (values: agree what success looks like using the partner’s own numbers; price rules: every number gets a source and a date; only publish numbers you can prove) plus the brief’s requirement that results are approved by the partner. Build 2026-11-03: both frames pass the lint (node 37:851) with no findings; the mobile frame has no layer wider than 390. Headings were set on balanced lines by hand (in code, text-wrap: balance). The 10% Ribbon Cyan row in the report preview is bound to Core/Ribbon Cyan with the resolved cyan as its base colour: the toolkit’s K.tint leaves the base colour black, which renders as a 10% black (grey) row. Review fix: the Tags on the placeholder card and in the report preview moved below their titles (the No Label Above rule); both frames re-linted with no findings. Outside review 2026-11-03: the hero note under the actions repeated the Until then lead almost word for word and took the hero past its budget, so it was removed (desktop 94:702, mobile 94:2796); the hero now holds one headline, one lead, one action group and one visual, and the ‘fictional company’ line stays in the Until then lead beside the sample report. Parts rows 3 and 4 restated rules 2 to 4 of the next section, so they now describe what the reader will find (results: figures such as time saved, money saved or earned, or fewer errors; quote: a short quote on what changed for their team) and the Rules section alone carries the source, date and approval promises. The mobile report preview (well 94:2886) cut through the second row’s text; it is now 301 px tall and crops at row 2’s bottom hairline. Both frames re-linted with no findings.
